source: Hitchcock, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: Critical Thinking (covers McPeck 1981, Ennis 1989, Abrami 2015)
finding: McPeck said there are no general thinking skills. Ennis answered that fields are vaguely bounded and inter-field principles exist (e.g. hypothetico-deductive reasoning). Three readings of subject-specificity: conceptual, epistemological, empirical. Mixed (separate plus embedded) instruction beat others in Abrami 2015 but not significantly.
numbers: No effect sizes in the excerpt. Cornell Level X credibility items: 24 of 76; Level Z experimental design items: 4 of 52. Dialogue, anchored instruction and mentoring each raised effectiveness.
quote: evidence for this claim is scanty
limits: Read through a fetch summary, last 15k characters not read. Most CT studies lack longitudinal follow-up.
agent_relevance: Do not assume one shared lesson store transfers. Key lessons by problem class; reuse elsewhere only after a check.

source: Gobet & Sala (2023) Cognitive Training: A Field in Search of a Phenomenon
finding: Second-order meta-analysis of 14 first-order meta-analyses finds far transfer from cognitive training is null once active controls and publication bias are handled.
numbers: 332 samples, 1,555 effect sizes, 21,968 participants. Uncorrected far-transfer g per meta-analysis 0.04 to 0.19, grand mean 0.12. Corrected, active controls only: -0.03 to 0.02, grand mean 0.00, true between-meta-analysis variance 0.
quote: The overall effect of far transfer is null
limits: Trains general abilities (working memory, video games, music, chess), not critical thinking. Authors take one side; a 48-researcher paper (Green et al. 2019) disagrees and was not opened.
agent_relevance: Strong prior that practice in one domain does not lift unrelated ones. Do not pool lessons across unrelated classes by default.

source: Gobet & Sala (2023), heterogeneity argument
finding: Apparent moderator effects across training types are mostly sampling error. True heterogeneity (tau squared) was near zero in almost every first-order analysis; the only real moderator found was control-group type.
numbers: Active-control table: tau squared 0.000 to 0.012. Second-order sampling-error variance 0.00302 versus observed between-meta-analysis variance 0.00014.
limits: Method claim from the same authors (Schmidt-Hunter artifact view).
agent_relevance: When our bench shows a lesson helping in one class, expect much of the variation to be noise. Confirm on held-out items before keying or sharing it.

source: Sala & Gobet (2017) Does Far Transfer Exist? Negative Evidence From Chess, Music, and Working Memory Training
finding: Three child-sample meta-analyses. Effects look small to moderate overall but shrink to near zero with active control groups.
numbers: Music: 0.25 SD [0.17,0.34] k=64 passive control vs 0.03 SD [-0.07,0.12] k=54 active control. WM training: 0.18 SD k=34 vs 0.05 SD [-0.05,0.15] k=40. Chess: one active-control study, 0.10 SD. Passive-control overall: chess 0.34 [0.24,0.44], music 0.16 [0.09,0.22].
quote: far transfer of learning rarely occurs
limits: Effects fall as design quality rises. Children and young adolescents only. Chess had too few active-control studies.
agent_relevance: Compare any lesson against an active control (neutral filler lesson), not only against no lesson.

source: Sala & Gobet (2017), common-elements account (Thorndike & Woodworth 1901)
finding: Common-elements theory: transfer scales with shared features, so near transfer is common and far transfer rare. A video-game study cited in the paper found gains stayed limited to the abilities the game targeted.
numbers: Chess players score half an SD above non-players on cognitive tests (a correlation), yet training does not reproduce the gap.
limits: Expertise-ability correlation is not causation. The video-game study is named in the text and was not opened.
agent_relevance: Supports reuse of a lesson when the new problem shares structure with the old one. Match by structure, not topic.

source: Working memory training transfer asymmetry meta-analysis (2026), Psychonomic Bulletin & Review
finding: Transfer is directional. Updating training transferred to span tasks, but span training did not transfer to updating tasks. Task similarity alone does not explain it.
numbers: 55 studies, 208 effect sizes, N = 3,492. Updating to span g = 0.176, p < .001. Span to updating g = 0.048, p = .453. Stronger at lower training doses, in non-adults, with verbal stimuli.
limits: Abstract and intro read; model details not checked. Near transfer between working memory tasks, not critical thinking.
agent_relevance: Transfer can be one-way. A lesson from the harder class may help the easier one but not the reverse; record direction.

source: Harapan et al. (2026) Does Inquiry-Based Learning Improve Students' Critical Thinking? A Meta-Analysis (F1000Research)
finding: Inquiry-based learning has a large pooled effect on critical thinking test scores. Subject domain did not moderate it.
numbers: 57 studies from 51 articles, 2015-2025. g = 1.336, 95% CI [1.061,1.611], I squared = 92.09%. Moderators: control group Qm = 5.21, p = .022; subject domain Qm = 1.43, p = .698; education level Qm = 1.11, p = .774; country Qm = 3.33, p = .650. Egger p < .001, funnel asymmetric.
limits: Implausibly large g, very high heterogeneity, small-study bias. Outcomes are CT test scores near the taught content, so near transfer. Non-significant moderator tests are weak evidence of domain-generality.
agent_relevance: Weak support for domain-general CT teaching. Treat large CT-instruction effects as near-transfer and inflated.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Reasoning or Reciting? Exploring the Capabilities and Limitations of Language Models Through Counterfactual Tasks
finding: Eleven task pairs share one procedure but change the mapping (base-9 arithmetic, rotated coordinates, altered chess rules). GPT-4 and others drop sharply from default to counterfactual, so skills are partly tied to the familiar version.
numbers: Two-digit addition, GPT-4: 100.0% base-10 vs 23.4% base-9 (no CoT); 98.2% vs 38.6% with 0-shot CoT. GPT-3.5: 100.0% vs 6.6%. Column grouping read from a table dump; could be off by one group.
limits: Counterfactual accuracy is still above chance, so some abstract skill exists. Execution budget and prompt design are arguable.
agent_relevance: A skill learned in the usual form can fail in a relabelled form. Store the conditions a lesson was learned under.

source: Wu et al. (2024), counterfactual comprehension checks and in-context demos
finding: Demonstrations in the counterfactual world did not close the default-counterfactual gap. Comprehension checks show the model often understands the new rules, so the failure is in applying a known procedure.
numbers: Comprehension check, GPT-4 base-9 addition: 90.0% (base-10 control 100.0%).
limits: Authors note a larger execution budget might help.
agent_relevance: Failure is applying a known procedure under a changed mapping. Code-side execution beats another prompt.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025) GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs (ICLR)
finding: Templated rewrites of grade-school math (new names or numbers) lower accuracy and widen variance. Adding one irrelevant but plausible clause (GSM-NoOp) causes large drops.
numbers: About 500 evaluations, 100 templates, 50 datasets per model. Gemma2-9B best-to-worst gap over 12 points. GSM-NoOp: Phi-3-mini drop over 65%, o1-preview -17.5, Gemma-7b-it about -20.6, Mistral-7b-v0.3 -24.0. Name-only changes hurt little; value changes hurt more.
limits: GPT-4o and Llama3-8B showed negligible drop on GSM-Symbolic, so contamination is not the whole story. Eight same-question shots did not fix NoOp. The 'cannot reason' reading is disputed.
agent_relevance: Surface changes break pattern matching. Mutated-input checks (G3) test that a result is not fitted to the surface.

source: Dziri et al. (2023) Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality
finding: Models solve compositional tasks by matching linearised subgraphs seen in training, not by learning a systematic procedure. Fine in distribution; wider or deeper problems fail.
numbers: 3-digit by 3-digit multiplication: ChatGPT 55%, GPT-4 59%. No gain in out-of-distribution generalisation past the overfitting point.
limits: Fine-tuning and theory parts not re-checked here.
agent_relevance: Expect failure on larger instances of a known class. Break such problems into code-checked sub-steps.

source: McCoy et al. (2024) Embers of Autoregression
finding: Accuracy depends on how common the task, input and output are, even for deterministic tasks. Rare variants of the same task fail more.
numbers: Shift cipher decoding: GPT-4 51% with high-probability output vs 13% with low-probability output. rot-13 encoding: 21% high-probability input vs 11% low-probability input. rot-13 is over 100 times more common online than rot-12.
limits: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 only, eleven tasks.
agent_relevance: Transfer to rare variants is where agents break. Send rare-variant problems to code or search, not recall.

source: Shojaee et al. (2025) The Illusion of Thinking
finding: Reasoning models show accuracy collapse past a complexity threshold on puzzles. Giving the solution algorithm in the prompt did not fix it.
numbers: Tower of Hanoi N=10 (about 1,000 moves): first error around move 100. River Crossing N=3 (11 moves): valid only to about move 4. Hanoi N=5 (31 moves) near perfect.
limits: Contested elsewhere: some argue output-length limits and unsolvable instances drive part of the collapse. Not resolved here.
agent_relevance: Knowing a procedure is not executing it reliably. The program executes; the model fills slots (section 1).

source: Zhao et al. (2026) Is Chain-of-Thought Reasoning of LLMs a Mirage? A Data Distribution Lens
finding: Models trained from scratch in a controlled environment show CoT works in distribution and collapses with shift in task, length or format. Small targeted fine-tuning recovers it only locally.
numbers: Exact match 100% in distribution; composition 0.01% (Qwen3-14B) and 8.52% (LLaMA3-8B); partial-OOD and OOD 0%. SFT recovery plateaus at the lower bound once edit distance reaches 3.
limits: Small models, synthetic data; may not carry to frontier models. Reasoning steps and answers often disagree.
agent_relevance: Transfer is local and stretches only a short distance. Supports narrow class keys.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet (ICLR)
finding: Without outside feedback, self-correction does not improve reasoning and often harms it. With oracle labels it helps a lot.
numbers: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 after one round. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5, 91.5, 89.0 over rounds. Oracle labels: GPT-4 GSM8K 97.5; HotpotQA 29.0 to 59.0. GPT-3.5 keeps its GSM8K answer 74.7% of the time.
limits: HotpotQA used 100 items. Oracle setting is an unrealistic upper bound.
agent_relevance: Reflection does not carry to new items unless grounded in real output (G2).

source: Zhou et al. (2022) Teaching Algorithmic Reasoning via In-Context Learning
finding: Explicit step-by-step algorithm demonstrations improve out-of-distribution length generalisation on arithmetic.
numbers: Error cut about 10x on long parity, 9x addition, 5x multiplication, 2x subtraction versus best baseline.
limits: Arithmetic only; needs detailed prompts. Contrasts with Shojaee et al., where a given algorithm did not help.
agent_relevance: Step-explicit demonstrations transfer better than slogans. Write lessons as steps.

source: Huan et al. (2025) Does Math Reasoning Improve General LLM Capabilities? Understanding Transferability of LLM Reasoning
finding: Of 20+ open reasoning models strong in math, many fail to carry the gains to other reasoning or non-reasoning tasks. Training method decides: RL on math transfers, SFT on math tends to forget.
numbers: Controlled Qwen3-14B-Base, math-only data. SFT-think scored 55.9% on GPQA; the RL model gained 1.8 on GPQA and 17.1 on LiveCodeBench2 over it. SFT models stagnate or decline on non-reasoning tasks; RL has positive Transferability Index.
limits: Open models and few recipes. Not about scaffolds.
agent_relevance: Domain-bound is the default for tuned models; do not assume a math lesson helps other classes.

source: Chu et al. (2025) SFT Memorizes, RL Generalizes
finding: Outcome-reward RL generalises to unseen rule variants and visual changes; SFT memorises.
numbers: RL: +3.5 points on GeneralPoints rule variant (11.5 to 15.0); +11.0 on V-IRL language variant (80.8 to 91.8); visual out-of-distribution +17.6 (23.6 to 41.2).
limits: Two environments. SFT still helps by stabilising output format.
agent_relevance: What generalises depends on the learning route; test transfer, never assume it.

source: Xie et al. (2025) Logic-RL: Unleashing LLM Reasoning with Rule-Based Reinforcement Learning
finding: A 7B model trained with rule-based RL on 5K synthetic logic puzzles gained on competition math it never saw.
numbers: AIME up 125% relative; AMC up 38% relative versus the base model.
limits: Relative gains from a low base; small AIME and AMC sets.
agent_relevance: Counterpoint to the human null: far transfer can appear in trained models. Not shown for scaffolds.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Reusable workflow memory helps in-domain and across tasks, websites and domains, with the largest edge where train-test gaps are widest.
numbers: Mind2Web with GPT-4, step success rate (cross-task / cross-website / cross-domain): MindAct 36.2 / 30.1 / 18.6; AWM offline 45.1 / 33.7 / 32.6; AWM online 43.6 / 33.9 / 35.5. Relative gains 24.6% Mind2Web, 51.1% WebArena.
limits: Whole-task success rates stay low (0.7 to 4.8). Online induction can store wrong workflows.
agent_relevance: Test-time lesson induction keeps lessons matched to the current class; supports class-keyed memory over a global store.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
finding: Insights extracted from HotpotQA transferred to FEVER when adapted by the model with a few demos.
numbers: FEVER success: Act 58, ReAct 63, ExpeL transfer without task demos 65, ExpeL transfer 70. Table layout was garbled; row order assumed.
limits: One source-target pair of closely related tasks (both Wikipedia lookup).
agent_relevance: Transfer worked where tools and structure were shared, as common-elements predicts.

source: Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory (2025)
finding: A self-curated memory of snippets raises accuracy across tasks, most when a reusable method (such as Python code) can be stored.
numbers: Claude 3.5 Sonnet: AIME 2020-24 6.7% to 40.6%; equation balancing 44.8% to 98-100%; GPQA-Diamond +9 points; MMLU-Pro Physics 74% to 82%. GPT-4o Game of 24 about 10% to 99%.
limits: Largest gains where the same method repeats; knowledge-heavy gains are smaller.
agent_relevance: Reuse works when problems share a solvable method; keying by class is consistent.

source: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory (2026)
finding: Memory of strategies from successes and failures generalises better than raw trajectories. Some baselines fail across sites.
numbers: WebArena Multi subset: +4.6 average success rate over strongest baseline, while AWM gave no gain and degraded. SWE-Bench Verified resolve rate: Gemini-2.5-flash 34.2 to 38.8; Gemini-2.5-pro 54.0 to 57.4.
limits: Authors' own method; limited test sets.
agent_relevance: Memory built on one site can hurt another; test cross-class transfer before pooling lessons.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) SELF-DISCOVER: LLMs Self-Compose Reasoning Structures
finding: The model composes task-specific reasoning structures from generic reasoning modules.
numbers: Average BBH +11% (GPT-4) and +7% (PaLM-2); T4D +39% and +29%; 10-40x less inference compute than self-consistency.
limits: Abstract-level figures; structure transfer between model families not checked in detail.
agent_relevance: Generic modules chosen per task is a middle path between all-general and all-specific skills.

source: Gick & Holyoak (1980, 1983) analogical problem solving
finding: From memory, not opened: few people spontaneously used a studied analogy on the radiation problem; most did after a hint; two examples and an abstract schema helped.
numbers: Recalled roughly: about 20-30% spontaneous vs about 90% after hint. Verify before citing.
limits: Not opened this session.
agent_relevance: Cueing the class matters more than merely having the lesson stored.

source: Abrami et al. (2015) Strategies for Teaching Students to Think Critically (Review of Educational Research)
finding: From memory, not opened: about 341 effect sizes, overall g+ near 0.30; dialogue, authentic problems and mentoring helped; mixed general-plus-infused teaching did best. The Stanford entry confirms the moderators but gives no numbers.
numbers: Recalled: g+ about 0.30. Verify.
limits: Not opened this session; Stanford entry says the mixed-instruction advantage was not significant.
agent_relevance: General principles plus domain examples is a design hint for a lesson store.

source: Halpern (1998) Teaching critical thinking for transfer across domains (American Psychologist)
finding: From memory, not opened: proposes dispositions, skills, structure training and metacognitive monitoring to get transfer; transfer needs cues to underlying structure.
limits: Found in a database listing only; text not read.
agent_relevance: Have the agent name the structure of a problem, then match it to stored lessons.

source: Willingham (2007) Critical Thinking: Why Is It So Hard to Teach? (American Educator)
finding: Page text did not load and the PDF fetch failed. From memory: thinking skills depend on domain knowledge, so transfer is hard.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Favours specifism: the skill rides on domain knowledge.
